steps.decide: Which columns carry decisions for the operator's job, and which are merely available
How sort, filter and pagination state are carried in the URL and announced
What each non-happy state says: empty-with-filters, empty-without-filters, loading, error, stale page
How the same records read at 390px without a horizontally scrolling row

rules.statement: A column earns its place by changing a decision; available data that changes nothing is removed from the default view, not shrunk.
Sort, filter and page live in the URL so a view can be shared and a refresh does not lose the operator's place.
Sorting and filtering announce the new result count and the active criteria through a live region, and keep focus in the toolbar.
No records yet and no records matching the filters are different states with different actions: create something, or clear the filters.
A failed page load keeps the previous rows visible with an inline error and a retry; clearing the table is never the error treatment.
Below the reflow threshold each record becomes a self-labelled block (table-to-card) with the same fields in the same order; horizontal scrolling for row data is prohibited for the launch set.
A row has one activation target; interactive cells stop the row from being clickable so a mis-click cannot both open a record and toggle a control.

sections.intent: Let an operator compare and act on records without losing their place in the list.
nicheDifferences: Support queues need SLA columns; finance needs amount alignment
Audit views need an immutable timestamp column
styling: Numeric columns right-aligned with tabular numerals
Row density chosen once per product
a11y: Real table semantics with scope on headers
Sort announced with the new order
responsive: No horizontal scrolling for row data
Card keeps the same field order as columns
copy: Column headers are nouns, not internal field names
alternatives: A list view is legitimate for five or fewer columns
Infinite scroll is not an alternative to pagination for operational work
